cards.explanation: The answer is the leaven of the Pharisees. Jesus says, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees…” (Luke 12:1). Leaven is what gets worked into dough, and in my line of work I know how far a little bit spreads. Notice He says it first to His disciples, with thousands of people packed around.

The answer is hypocrisy. Jesus gives it Himself: the leaven of the Pharisees is “hypocrisy” (Luke 12:1). He doesn't leave His disciples guessing, which I appreciate, because I've guessed wrong on a recipe card before. Hypocrisy is looking one way on the outside while being something else on the inside.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.” (Luke 12:2). No exceptions on that list, friends. I once tried hiding a burnt batch under a dish towel, and the smell told on me before the timer even stopped.

The answer is that they can do no more. Jesus says not to be afraid of those who kill the body “…and after that can do no more.” (Luke 12:4). He's talking to His friends here, and He picks His words carefully. Their reach has an end, and He says where it is.

The answer is the One with authority to throw them into hell. Jesus says, “Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!” (Luke 12:5). He says it plainly, and He even says it twice in a way. This is a heavy part, and I think He wants His friends to hear it clearly.
The answer is True. Jesus asks, “Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.” (Luke 12:6). Cheap in the market, not forgotten by God. That's what He says.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.” (Luke 12:7). He just finished saying not one sparrow is forgotten by God, then tells His friends they're worth more than many of them. That's a lot of reasons not to be afraid.

The answer is before the angels of God. Jesus says, “…everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.” (Luke 12:8). Someone claims Him in front of people, and He claims them in front of the angels of God. I think that's a promise worth holding on to.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.” (Luke 12:9). It's the other side of the verse before it. Claiming Him and denying Him both get an answer before the angels of God.

The answer is the Holy Spirit. Jesus says, “…whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.” (Luke 12:10). Just before that, He says everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven. That's a serious line, friends.

The word is defend. Jesus says, “…do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.” (Luke 12:11). He's talking about being brought before synagogues, rulers and authorities. He tells them not to worry, and that's a relief to a nervous talker like me.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.” (Luke 12:12). The disciples don't have to cook up the words alone. The Holy Spirit teaches them at that time.
